title: Data Quality Detective
creator: Hank Ratzesberger & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Seven cases of multi-channel station data on a shared time axis with a log strip and a comparison-station overlay, each containing exactly one anomaly, scored on both the diagnosis and the evidence cited for it.

learningObjectives: Differentiate instrument faults from real environmental events.
Justify a diagnosis by checking whether other channels moved consistently.
Recognise sensor drift, which no single reading reveals.
Apply the flag-do-not-delete rule to suspect data.
prerequisites: Chapter 15: outliers, missing data, drift and validation
Chapter 6 on radiation shields; Chapter 9 on cloud-edge enhancement

keyQuestions: If one channel moves and the others do not, what does that tell you?
How would you detect a fault that no single reading reveals?
Is every real reading a weather observation?
Should a suspect row be deleted or flagged?
commonMisconceptions: An extreme reading is always an error.
A fault can be diagnosed from the channel it appears in.
Bad data should be deleted from the file.
Any irradiance reading above the clear-sky value must be a fault.
assessmentOpportunities: Diagnoses each case and cites only the evidence that actually holds.
Solves the drift case using the comparison overlay.
Distinguishes the breathing case from the frontal passage and explains both.
